## Evidence and ranking method

This record captures NP_Labs results released by George Awad on September 28,
2026, and the participant-only leaderboard files supplied on September 29.
The original ZIPs, MC text file, and AG workbook are preserved unchanged in
this directory, with SHA-256 checksums in [the manifest](attachment-manifest.json).
The supplied MC ZIP is byte-identical to the one recovered from the email.

Ranks below are calculated from organizer scores: descending competition rank
(1 plus the number of strictly better runs). Ties share a rank and leave gaps.
AG comparisons use the workbook's six-decimal score precision. There are
42 MC runs and 44 AG runs per reference mode. These are run ranks, not team
ranks; the source files do not supply an explicit run-to-team mapping.
No single overall AG ranking is inferred across metrics or reference modes.

[Full extracted leaderboards and metric ranks](leaderboard-summary.json)
retain all rows and source coordinates. All 216 local AG aggregate fields match
the workbook within 0.00000051, and all four MC summaries agree with the
leaderboard at its reported precision.

## MC results

All four NP_Labs runs scored 2,428 queries after 15 exclusions from 2,443,
with no missing scored queries, warnings, or errors.

| Run | Correct | Accuracy | Accuracy rank / 42 | MRR | MRR rank / 42 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| g37_mc_direct | 2052 | 84.514% | 2 | 0.905653 | 3 |
| g38_mc_direct | 2047 | 84.308% | 3 (tie) | 0.905368 | 4 |
| g37_mc_target | 2025 | 83.402% | 8 | 0.896845 | 8 |
| g37q36_mc_text | 1912 | 78.748% | 26 | 0.864605 | 23 |

Our best accuracy run, `g37_mc_direct`, is six correct answers behind the accuracy leader `isu-mc-fusefga-v2n` (2,058 correct). The MRR leader is `NII_UIT-avg2_q38` (0.908122). These are descriptive differences; statistical significance has not been assessed.

| q36_dualview | human_answer_only | 0.446630 (28) | 0.175050 (40) | 0.887815 (19) |
| g37_grouped_unique | all_references | 0.484527 (19, tie) | 0.318244 (2, tie) | 0.878867 (39, tie) |
| g37_q36_fusion | all_references | 0.484527 (19, tie) | 0.318244 (2, tie) | 0.878867 (39, tie) |
| q35_4b_u12 | all_references | 0.485552 (17) | 0.170537 (44) | 0.890737 (22) |
| q36_dualview | all_references | 0.465828 (28) | 0.188578 (41) | 0.891633 (19) |

The two g37 runs tie for second on METEOR@1 in both reference modes.
Their top-1 scores match, but their scores at other cutoffs differ. The full
JSON preserves all 27 metrics per run per reference mode. The workbook defines
NDCG as ranking quality within submitted answers using metric scores as graded
relevance; it is not a cross-team answer-correctness measure. Higher is better
for all workbook effectiveness metrics. Missing answer ranks count as zero in
mean-top-k scores.

## How our approaches work

### Answer generation: produce and order answers

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    V["Video + question"] --> G["Gemini 3.7 Flash<br/>Native audio/video answer"]
    V --> Q["Qwen3.6<br/>Video with and without transcript"]
    V --> C["Qwen3.5-4B<br/>12 uniform frames"]
    G --> F["g37_q36_fusion<br/>Valid Gemini answer first<br/>Qwen alternatives below"]
    Q --> F
    C --> F
    Q --> D["q36_dualview<br/>Combine Qwen views"]
    C --> B["q35_4b_u12<br/>Baseline answer list"]
    F --> R["g37_grouped_unique<br/>Group meanings and rewrite<br/>Keep first answer unchanged"]
```

These are four separately submitted AG runs. Fusion uses Qwen/control
fallbacks when Gemini fails or is unavailable. Grouped rewriting is text-only
and uses frozen source answers; it does not re-examine the video. The diagram
summarizes the flow, not every repair or fallback operation.

**Why this matters:** top-1 metrics inspect only the first answer. Having a
better answer lower in the list cannot improve those metrics. The grouped
variant preserves the fusion first answer, so their identical top-1 scores
are expected. Whether our ordering actually left better answers below rank
one requires per-query analysis; it is not established by this diagram.

### Multiple choice: rank the supplied options

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    I["Question + official answer options"] --> T["Text selector<br/>Gemini 3.7 + frozen AG answer"]
    T --> V1["g37q36_mc_text<br/>78.748% accuracy"]
    I --> A["Blind text audit<br/>Select 798 queries to revisit"]
    A --> V2["g37_mc_target<br/>Video rankings on selected queries<br/>Text rankings elsewhere<br/>83.402% accuracy"]
    I --> G["Gemini direct video ranking<br/>Native audio/video + options"]
    M["Video and audio"] --> G
    G --> V2
    G --> V3["g37_mc_direct<br/>Full Gemini 3.7 pass<br/>84.514% accuracy"]
    G --> V4["g38_mc_direct<br/>Separate Gemini 3.8 pass + retry<br/>84.308% accuracy"]
    T -.->|"Fallback when direct ranking fails"| V2
    T -.->|"Fallback when direct ranking fails"| V3
    T -.->|"Fallback when direct ranking fails"| V4
```

The direct Gemini 3.7 pass uses 4 FPS, low media resolution, and high thinking.
Its frozen direct predictions supply both the targeted and full 3.7 runs;
Gemini 3.8 is a separate pass. The audit sees the frozen AG answer, question,
and options, but not the text selector's ranking. Counts such as the 798-query
audit queue describe the 2,443-query submission panel; reported accuracies
use the 2,428-query scored panel.

**Why MC can be stronger:** it sees the candidate answers while examining
video evidence. AG must produce its own answer and choose its wording. This
explains a task difference, not a proven cause of the metric gaps. AG
similarity scores must not be read as correctness percentages or compared
numerically with MC accuracy.

## Organizer instructions

- **Speaker proposal due October 12, 2026**, preferably earlier. Include talk
  title; speaker name, email and affiliation; registered team name; and
  in-person or virtual presentation mode.
- **Workshop: November 16–18, 2026.** Organizers also plan to present their
  2027 track proposal.
- **Registration:** $400 in person or $225 student, closing November 2;
  $60 virtual, closing November 18 at noon (timezone not specified in email).
- The organizer announced plans to update the VQA repository with the scorer
  used for 2026. Availability of that code has not been verified here.
- August 26 instructions superseded the original MC query file with Task2_v2:
  incorrect extra answer options were fixed, options reshuffled, and punctuation
  normalized. Task 2 uses the same videos as Task 1.
- The August 10 notice required retaining unavailable-video queries in AG
  submissions for validation, while excluding them from scoring. Recovered
  results confirm 2,428 scored queries. No paper deadline was supplied in the
  reviewed results emails; October 12 is the speaker-proposal deadline.

## Scope and remaining work

The source files, scores, leaderboard comparisons, and organizer instructions
are captured. No inference was rerun and no submission files were changed.
This record does not establish model-family causality or statistical
significance. Mapping run identifiers to exact submitted configurations is a
separate analysis. No release or public publication was created.
